rationale: The assistant reached the right end point quickly: socket and fuse ruled out, cable inspected, then a clear hand-off to Candy support or the warranty provider with an explicit statement that nothing further is user-serviceable. However it made some dubious technical claims stated as fact ('The most common cause in Candy washer-dryers after a power cut is the internal mains fuse blowing on the PCB or within the mains lead assembly itself', 'opened during the surge' when the customer never confirmed a surge) and nudged toward a continuity check the homeowner could not reasonably perform. It never asked for the model number, door closure or consumer unit/RCD status, and did not name the mains suppression filter as an alternative to the board, but the diagnosis stayed hedged with 'likely' and no part purchase was pushed.
